title: Flexible Thermal Conductance Model (TCM) for Efficient Thermal Simulation of 3-D ICs and Packages
problem: Thermal simulation of 3D ICs and packages is computationally expensive, requiring large solution domains and extensive simulations despite the fact that only specific regions (ROI) contain key thermal design components.
motivation: Thermal management is increasingly critical as 3D IC complexity grows, requiring accurate and efficient thermal evaluation for design optimization.
method: The method partitions the structure into Region of Interest (ROI) and Region of Fixity (ROF), constraining the solution domain to the ROI. A flexible thermal conductance model (TCM) with rational expressions represents the thermal impact of ROF as boundary conditions, enabling efficient handling of varying boundary conditions.
key_novelty: Flexible TCM with elegant rational expressions for heat convection coefficients that adapts to varying boundary conditions while constraining computation to ROI.
contributions: Flexible boundary condition handling for varying thermal scenarios
Significant reduction in computational domain and memory requirements
limitations: Limitations not discussed in abstract; applicability to extreme 3D stacking scenarios unclear.
